public_rationale: The identified tracker does not validate the comparison as written. Its February commentary describes 190 GW overall, then discusses 5 GW under construction within the capacity scheduled for 2026. A March Crusoe announcement also identifies a major customer, complicating the demand assertion. Neither source supplies the matched March construction totals, financing records and demand evidence needed to settle the whole claim.
limitations: The tracker snapshot predates the selected observation window.
The tracker includes large data centers and AI factories, rather than an explicitly AI-only population.
A named customer does not prove sufficient ultimate demand or profitable operation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Debt-funded data center companies have started 200GW of projects, only 5GW under construction, for AI demand that does not exist.

statement.excerpt: The AI data center companies that, thanks to readily-available debt, have started 200GW of projects (and only started building 5GW of them) for AI demand that doesn’t exist, entirely based on the theoretical sense that maybe it will in the future.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: entirely based on the theoretical sense that maybe it will in the future
our_interpretation: Read 'started projects' as announced or initiated development, distinguished from physical construction.
Treat 200 GW and 5 GW as approximate totals for the same project population.
Use March 2026, through the post date, as the current-state reporting window. The speaker supplies no tracker date.
Read the demand assertion as saying these projects lack existing commercial demand sufficient to underpin their development. Merely showing that some people use AI would not rebut it.
The claim also attributes project initiation to accessible debt; capacity totals alone cannot establish that explanation.
criteria.support_condition: A contemporaneous, consistently defined project inventory shows approximately 200 GW initiated and approximately 5 GW under construction, with financing and customer records showing that readily available debt enabled projects unsupported by existing commercial demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially contradict either capacity total, or establish substantial existing commercial demand underpinning the identified project population. Evidence that debt did not enable the projects would contradict the financing explanation.

evidence.excerpt: Yet only about 5GW is currently under construction.
evidence.explanation: The surrounding paragraph distinguishes a 190 GW total pipeline from 16 GW scheduled for 2026; the 5 GW figure concerns that scheduled subset. This earlier snapshot does not establish that only 5 GW of the entire pipeline was under construction in March.

evidence.excerpt: We're excited to welcome Microsoft to the Abilene community.
evidence.locator: Quotation from Abilene mayor Weldon Hurt
evidence.explanation: The announcement identifies Microsoft as the customer for a new Abilene campus. That challenges a literal absence-of-customers reading, but neither establishes membership in the claimed tracker population nor proves sufficient, sustainable end demand.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated March project inventory with consistent capacity and construction definitions, linked financing records, and customer commitments for the same projects.
